## Mains side

> **MAINS VOLTAGE. This design has NOT been safety-certified, tested or inspected by anyone.** The mains side (inlet, fuse, relay module, supply terminals, protective earth) must be wired, or checked before first power, by a person competent to do so under your local rules. The electrical verifier checks ratings and that the wires exist; it does not check creepage, enclosure, strain relief, touch protection, or any standard.

- Supply voltage declared: (115.0, 230.0) V. Mains current {'115': 4.65, '230': 2.32} A; inlet rated 10.0 A; fuse T8A (time-lag); cold-start inrush 60.0 A (the fuse riding through it was assumed, I2t not checked).
- **Set the supply's 115 / 230 V selector switch to your mains before first power.** It is on the supply's side; the wrong position destroys the supply (230 V on the 115 V setting).
- The inlet's fuse drawer and fuse-link are ordered separately from the inlet (see BOM.md).
- Live terminals that are open to touch in this open-frame design: the inlet's rear quick-connect tabs, the relay module's screw terminals and solder side, the supply's terminal block. **No cover for any of them is in the design.** Fit covers or an enclosure before the machine is powered with hands near it.

### Relay and neutral

The relay module switches the LIVE only and powers its own coil electronics from the mains, so the NEUTRAL is looped through its `N` terminal: one wire inlet N to relay N, a second relay N to supply N, both in one twin ferrule in the relay's N terminal. Without the neutral at the relay it never pulls in. The control board's `PS-ON` pin holds the relay in while the firmware runs and drops it on any shutdown: that relay is the only cut-off for a hotend heater whose MOSFET has failed short (report warning `cutoff_depends_on_mcu`: it does not act if the controller itself has hung).

### Protective earth

- Earth wires in the model: earth to supply (inlet PE to the supply's FG terminal) and earth to frame (inlet PE to the frame stud).
- Frame stud: `earth_stud`, an M5 screw into a T-nut in the outer slot of `frame_bot_left`, ring terminal and star washer under its head; scratch through the anodising under the washer (crimp ring terminals; scratch through the anodising under the washer).
- **The model bonds ONE extrusion.** Every other frame member, the electronics tray, the inlet panel, the motors' bodies, the gantry and the bed carrier are earthed only through anodised extrusion joints, T-nuts, linear bearings or lead-screw nuts, none of which is a reliable bond. Before first power measure continuity from the inlet's earth pin to: each extrusion, the tray, the inlet panel, the supply's case, each motor body, the X beam, the bed plate. Anything above about 0.1 ohm needs its own earth wire. The bed heater is 24 V, but a mains fault to the frame must still blow the fuse.

- **Inconsistency in the model:** the earth point's port is declared `ring-M4` and the BOM buys an M4 ring terminal, but the stud is an SHCS-M5x8 screw. An M4 ring does not go over an M5 screw: buy an M5 ring terminal.

## Declared but not drawn as wires

- `bed_probe`: its supply (24.0 V, from '24 V rail at the control board's power terminals') is declared on the device and **not routed as a wire**: no length, no BOM quantity, no loom check for the + lead. Its 0 V return is carried in the signal cable's conductor count.
- `bed_probe`: a series diode (BAT85 class, cathode to the sensor) is declared in the signal lead; where it is mounted (at the board connector, in the loom) is not modelled.
- `Y motor left`: mirror-image motor: swap one coil pair at the connector so both turn the belts the same way

## Firmware configuration

`printer.cfg` in this folder is a copy of `out/printer_v8/electrical/printer.cfg`, generated from the electrical model and loaded by real Klipper in batch mode (klippy ran: True, ok: True, commit 29d4ec2d; that covers: klippy loads every section and plans moves on it; homing and probing against real switches are not exercised).

It holds only what the model knows. Add your host's sections (`[virtual_sdcard]`, `[pause_resume]`, `[display_status]`, macros) yourself. Firmware coordinates: X [0.0, 180.0], Y [34.5, 214.5] is the print area (set the slicer's bed origin and size to match: Y does not start at 0 because the axis has extra travel for the probe).

### Values that must be measured or tuned on the real machine

| Where in printer.cfg | Value in the file | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| [extruder] pid_Kp/Ki/Kd | pid_Kp 43.601; pid_Ki 18.167; pid_Kd 26.161 | `PID_CALIBRATE HEATER=extruder TARGET=<print temp>` with the part fan at print speed; the values in the file come from a simulated autotune |
| [heater_bed] pid_Kp/Ki/Kd | pid_Kp 70.226; pid_Ki 4.682; pid_Kd 263.347 | `PID_CALIBRATE HEATER=heater_bed TARGET=60`; simulated values, heater tolerance +/-10 % not modelled |
| [input_shaper] shaper_type/freq, damping_ratio | shaper_type_x ei; shaper_type_y mzv; shaper_freq_x 100.6; shaper_freq_y 59.8; damping_ratio_x 0.065; damping_ratio_y 0.069 | measure with an accelerometer on the toolhead (`SHAPER_CALIBRATE`); the file holds the twin's prediction |
| [extruder] pressure_advance | pressure_advance 0.0420; pressure_advance_smooth_time 0.04 | print a pressure-advance tower / pattern; the file holds the twin's sweep result |
| [probe] z_offset | z_offset 3.000 | `PROBE_CALIBRATE` with the bed and nozzle at working temperature; the file's value assumes the nominal switching distance on iron |
| [probe] x_offset / y_offset | x_offset 0; y_offset 34.5 | confirm by probing a known feature or a mark; values are from the CAD |
| [bed_mesh] | [bed_mesh] present | `BED_MESH_CALIBRATE` hot; compare the range with the prediction in COMMISSIONING.md |
| [stepper_*] rotation_distance | rotation_distance stepper_x: 40; rotation_distance stepper_y: 40; rotation_distance stepper_z: 2 | command 100 mm, measure with a rule / calipers / dial indicator; belts: 40 = 20 teeth x 2 mm; Z: the screw's lead |
| [extruder] rotation_distance / gear_ratio | rotation_distance 26.8937; gear_ratio 11.262:1 | mark filament, extrude 100 mm slowly, measure; the values are E3D's published figures |
| [tmc2209 *] run_current | run_current stepper_x: 0.280; run_current stepper_y: 1.200; run_current stepper_z: 1.000; run_current extruder: 0.400 | the design's choices; check motor case temperature after 30 min (predictions in COMMISSIONING.md) and that no axis loses steps |
| [stepper_*] dir_pin | dir_pin stepper_x: !PB12; dir_pin stepper_y: PC5; dir_pin stepper_z: !PB2 | `STEPPER_BUZZ` each motor and jog each axis: invert where the direction is wrong. The left Y motor is a mirror image: one coil pair swapped at its connector |
| [stepper_x/y] position_endstop, position_min/max | not present | after the switches are set (ASSEMBLY.md), home and measure the real travel to the other end |
| [stepper_z] position_min | position_min -1.550 | negative by the declared Z over-travel; confirm the bed can physically rise that far past the nozzle plane without anything else touching |
| [verify_heater *] | [verify_heater extruder] present; [verify_heater heater_bed] present | leave as generated unless a false trip occurs; never loosen to hide a real fault |
| [mcu] serial | serial /dev/ttyAMA0 | the host's UART device as wired (TFT header); check `ls /dev/serial*` |

### printer.cfg

```ini
# printer.cfg for printer_v8: GENERATED by mechloop from the electrical model. Do not edit by hand;
# change the design and regenerate. Directions (dir_pin '!') and the extruder rotation_distance must be
# confirmed on the machine; PID values come from a simulated PID_CALIBRATE and should be re-run on the real heater.
# Input shaper, pressure advance and probe offsets below are PREDICTIONS from the simulation, each resting on
# assumed values named beside it: re-measure on the machine (SHAPER_CALIBRATE, a pressure-advance test print,
# PROBE_CALIBRATE, BED_MESH_CALIBRATE).

[mcu]
serial: /dev/ttyAMA0
restart_method: command

[printer]
kinematics: cartesian
max_velocity: 250
max_accel: 4000
max_z_velocity: 12
max_z_accel: 200

[stepper_x]
step_pin: PB13
dir_pin: !PB12
enable_pin: !PB14
microsteps: 16
rotation_distance: 40
endstop_pin: ^PC0
position_endstop: 0
position_min: 0
position_max: 180
homing_speed: 50

[tmc2209 stepper_x]
uart_pin: PC11
tx_pin: PC10
uart_address: 0
run_current: 0.280
sense_resistor: 0.110
stealthchop_threshold: 0

[stepper_y]
step_pin: PB0
dir_pin: PC5
enable_pin: !PB1
microsteps: 16
rotation_distance: 40
endstop_pin: ^PC1
position_endstop: 214.5
position_min: 0
position_max: 214.5
homing_speed: 50
homing_positive_dir: true

[tmc2209 stepper_y]
uart_pin: PC11
tx_pin: PC10
uart_address: 1
run_current: 1.200
sense_resistor: 0.110
stealthchop_threshold: 0

[stepper_z]
step_pin: PB10
dir_pin: !PB2
enable_pin: !PB11
microsteps: 16
rotation_distance: 2
endstop_pin: probe:z_virtual_endstop
position_min: -1.550
position_max: 183.100
homing_speed: 5
second_homing_speed: 1
homing_retract_dist: 3

[tmc2209 stepper_z]
uart_pin: PC11
tx_pin: PC10
uart_address: 2
run_current: 1.000
sense_resistor: 0.110
stealthchop_threshold: 0

[extruder]
step_pin: PB3
dir_pin: !PB4
enable_pin: !PD1
microsteps: 16
rotation_distance: 26.8937
gear_ratio: 11.262:1
full_steps_per_rotation: 400
nozzle_diameter: 0.400
filament_diameter: 1.750
heater_pin: PC8
sensor_type: ATC Semitec 104NT-4-R025H42G
sensor_pin: PA0
control: pid
pid_Kp: 43.601
pid_Ki: 18.167
pid_Kd: 26.161
min_temp: 0
max_temp: 280
max_extrude_only_distance: 100
max_extrude_only_velocity: 60
max_extrude_only_accel: 3000
# pressure advance: best of a sweep on the twin (smallest corner bulge + recess), whose melt-flow lag is 32 ms (direct drive, 0.4 mm nozzle: factory pressure-advance values (fitted_parameters.json: extruder_lag_s), range 0.02 to 0.058 s); not measured on this machine: print a pressure-advance test
pressure_advance: 0.0420
pressure_advance_smooth_time: 0.04

[tmc2209 extruder]
uart_pin: PC11
tx_pin: PC10
uart_address: 3
run_current: 0.400
sense_resistor: 0.110

[heater_bed]
heater_pin: PC9
sensor_type: Generic 3950
sensor_pin: PC4
control: pid
pid_Kp: 70.226
pid_Ki: 4.682
pid_Kd: 263.347
min_temp: 0
max_temp: 90

[verify_heater extruder]
max_error: 120
check_gain_time: 20
hysteresis: 5
heating_gain: 2

[verify_heater heater_bed]
max_error: 120
check_gain_time: 60
hysteresis: 5
heating_gain: 2

[fan]
pin: PC6

# fan 'hotend_fan' is wired to the board's +5 V rail: it runs whenever the machine is powered (no firmware section)

# mains relay ahead of the 24 V supply: energised while the firmware runs, dropped on any shutdown
[output_pin ps_on]
pin: PC13
value: 1
shutdown_value: 0

# input shaper: predicted by the twin, not measured: resonance X 79.7 Hz, Y 59.4 Hz (belt stiffness only, no FEA frame stiffness); damping assumed. Run SHAPER_CALIBRATE
[input_shaper]
shaper_type_x: ei
shaper_freq_x: 100.6
damping_ratio_x: 0.065
shaper_type_y: mzv
shaper_freq_y: 59.8
damping_ratio_y: 0.069

# probe: offsets from the CAD; z_offset from the probe's nominal switching distance on steel (5.0 mm) - set it on the machine with PROBE_CALIBRATE
# that distance: OMRON E2E data sheet CSM_E2E_DS_E_12_4: 5 mm +/-10 % on the standard iron target
[probe]
pin: ^!PC2
x_offset: 0
y_offset: 34.5
z_offset: 3.000
speed: 5
lift_speed: 10
samples: 3
samples_result: median
sample_retract_dist: 2
samples_tolerance: 0.04
samples_tolerance_retries: 3

# Z homes with the probe over the middle of the bed
[safe_z_home]
home_xy_position: 90, 90
speed: 100
z_hop: 5
z_hop_speed: 5

# mesh bounds are probe positions: the bed inset by the probe's edge margin, cut to where the probe can reach
[bed_mesh]
speed: 100
horizontal_move_z: 5
mesh_min: 0, 34.5
mesh_max: 180, 222.5
probe_count: 5, 5
algorithm: lagrange
mesh_pps: 2, 2
fade_start: 1
fade_end: 10
fade_target: 0
split_delta_z: 0.01
zero_reference_position: 90, 124.5
```
